Q0.p: A general heading for motifs in which good and bad behavior are followed by reward or punishment.

Q1.p: A person who shows hospitality is rewarded, and the opposite behavior, refusing hospitality, is punished.

Q1.1.r: *Types 750AB, 751, 750*; *BP II 210, III 206; Aarne FFC XXIII 46; *Dh II 117; *Fb “Sankt Peder” III 164b, “rig” III 55a.—Spanish: Espinosa II No. 86, III Nos. 168—171, Espinosa Jr. No. 181; India: *Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera II 656; Japanese: Ikeda.
Q1.1.p: Gods or saints in disguise travel as beggars, rewarding those who welcome them and punishing those who turn them away. Usually the hospitable person is poor and the inhospitable one is rich.

Q2.p: A rude person ignores the requests of an old person or an animal and is punished, while a courteous person, often the youngest brother or sister, complies and is rewarded.

Q3.r: India: Thompson-Balys; Japanese: Ikeda; West Indies: Flowers 566.
Q3.p: A reward goes to the person who asks for a modest amount, while the greedy person who asks for too much is punished.

Q3.1.r: Wienert FFC LVI 79* (ET 449), 139 (ST 444); Halm Aesop No. 308; Lithuanian: Balys Index No. 729*; Chinese: Eberhard FFC CXX 34 No. 20; Japanese: Ikeda.
Q3.1.p: A woodsman drops his axe in the water and a god brings him gold and silver axes, which he refuses as not his. He is rewarded for honesty with his own axe, while a greedy companion who copies him loses his axe.

Q3.2.p: A thief demands half of a stolen bullock, and a modest traveler who withdraws is then invited to take half, so the greedy claimant is shown up.

Q4.p: The humble are rewarded and the proud or arrogant are punished.

Q5.p: Lazy people are punished and hardworking people are rewarded.

Q5.1.p: A lazy jackal is punished while an industrious pig is rewarded.

Q5.2.p: A lazy owl is punished while an industrious hummingbird is rewarded.

Q6.p: People who think good thoughts are rewarded, and those who think bad thoughts are punished.

Q6.1.p: Foolishness leads a man to death, while a calm, quiet disposition brings good fortune.

Q7.p: A deity comes down and makes the king and a wronged subject switch places, so the wrong is set right.

Q20.r: Irish: *Cross, O’Suilleabhain 120, Beal XXI 336; Spanish Exempla: Keller; Jewish: *Neuman; India: *Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera II 1153; Hawaii: Beckwith Myth 70.
Q20.p: Piety, or devout religious conduct, is rewarded.

Q20.1.p: A god, hero, or ascetic is rewarded for serving them for a set period of time.

Q20.2.p: Keeping religious rules or commandments is rewarded.

Q21.p: A person who makes a religious sacrifice is rewarded.

Q21.1.p: A poor old woman gives her only cow, trusting God to repay her a hundred times over. A bishop hears of her faith and sends her a hundred cows.

Q23.p: A person who wins others over to the faith is rewarded.

Q25.r: (St. Christopher.) *Type 768; Dh II 266; Legenda Aurea (ed. Graesse) 432; *Schwickert Zs. f. Vksk. NF III 14—26; Klapper Erzählungen des Mittelalters 111 No. 101; *Loomis White Magic 114.
Q25.p: A person is rewarded for carrying Christ across a stream, and Christ appears in the form of a child.

Q25.1.r: Leper is Christ in disguise. Irish myth: Cross.
Q25.1.p: A boy risks his life carrying a leper across a stream.

Q26.p: A person who fasts (goes without food as a religious act) is given a reward.

Q27.p: A boy who is doomed to die is saved by a miracle because of his faith.

Q28.p: A person who makes a religious pilgrimage to a holy place is rewarded.

Q32.p: A person who gives food to a crucifix or an image of the Madonna is rewarded.

Q33.r: (Cf. V50.) Ward II 621 No. 30; Scala Celi 136b No. 760; Jewish: *Neuman; India: *Thompson-Balys.
Q33.p: A person who says prayers is rewarded.

Q34.r: (Cf. Q144.1.) The further he must carry water, the greater his heavenly reward. Scala Celi 15a No. 84; Oesterley No. 80; *A. E. Schönbach Die Legende von Engel und Waldbruder (Wien, 1901); India: *Thompson-Balys.
Q34.p: A hermit who practices severe self-denial and penance is rewarded for it.

Q35.p: A person who writes a religious hymn is rewarded.

Q36.p: A person who repents of wrongdoing is rewarded.

Q36.1.p: A person who confesses their sins is rewarded.

Q37.p: A person who carries out a dead man's request is rewarded.

Q38.r: (Cf. Q116.1.) Jewish: Neuman; Chinese: Eberhard FFC CXX 83, 158, 163f.
Q38.p: A person who serves or waits upon a holy man is rewarded.

Q39.p: Miscellaneous rewards for piety that do not fit the more specific headings above.

Q39.1.r: (Cf. V462.) Buddhist myth: Malalasekera I 500, II 750.
Q39.1.p: A person who practices asceticism, meaning strict self-denial for religious reasons, is rewarded.

Q40.r: *Chauvin VI 109 No. 274 n. 2; Irish: Beal XXI 304; Missouri French: Carrière; Greek: Fox 200 (Phaon); Buddhist myth: Malalasekera I 362; Chinese: Graham, Eberhard FFC CXX 132 No. 87; Africa (Bankon): Ittman 83, (Bulu): Krug 109, (Duala): Lederbogen JAS IV 71.
Q40.p: A person who shows kindness to others is rewarded.

Q41.r: *Roberts 173; Icelandic: Boberg; Breton: Sébillot Incidents s.v. “politesse”; Missouri French: Carrière; Spanish: Espinosa III No. 152, Espinosa Jr. Nos. 117, 130, 183; Italian: Basile Pentamerone IV Nos. 7, 8.
Q41.p: A person who is polite or courteous is rewarded.

Q41.1.p: An ogre is calmed and pleased when someone addresses it as uncle or aunt, a flattering family title.

Q41.2.r: *Roberts 168; Type 480; Africa (Chaga): Gutmann 132ff. No. 83, (Alo): Pratt-Chadwick and Lamprey The Alo Man (New York, 1927) 17ff., (Batanga): Nassau JAFL XXVIII 45ff. No. 16, (Bulu): Krug JAFL XXV 113 No. 9, (Bambara): Travélé 205ff. No. 66, (Hausa): Equilbecq Contes indigènes III 291ff., Tremearne Hausa Superstitions and Customs (London, 1913) 424ff. No. 93.
Q41.2.p: A person is rewarded for cleaning a loathsome or filthy person, such as by cleansing their eyelids, bathing them, or removing lice.

Q42.r: *Chauvin V 14 No. 68; *Penzer VIII 130ff.; Irish myth: Cross; Breton: Sébillot Incidents s.v. “charité”; Spanish: Keller, Espinosa III No. 152, Espinosa Jr. Nos. 202—204, 210; India: *Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera II 897, 904, 934, 988; Tahiti: Beckwith Myth 38.
Q42.p: A person who is generous and gives freely to others is rewarded.

Q42.1.r: *Types 508, 592, 665; BP II 490ff., Scala Celi 81b No. 467; *Hibbard 73, 79; Alphabet No. 291; Japanese: Anesaki 320.
Q42.1.p: A spendthrift knight gives away his last penny to someone in need, and is later helped by that grateful person.

Q42.1.1.p: A child shares their last loaf of bread with a fairy, witch, or similar supernatural being, and is rewarded for it.

Q42.1.1.1.p: A child who shares their last loaf of bread with a fairy, witch, or similar being is rewarded for the generosity.

Q42.1.2.p: A man who shares his food with a beggar is later freed from captivity by that beggar.

Q42.1.3.p: A chieftain who is so hospitable that he gives away too much becomes poor as a result.

Q42.2.p: A person who provides coffins for the poor is rewarded for this charitable act.

Q42.3.r: (Cf. Q1, Q45.1.) Alphabet Nos. 297, 344, 365; Scala Celi 39b No. 222; Irish: Beal XXI 304, 325, O’Suilleabhain 2, 68; Spanish: Keller, Espinosa II No. 86, III Nos. 168—171, Espinosa Jr. Nos. 83—85, 181f., 210; India: *Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera I 485; Chinese: Graham.
Q42.3.p: A person who shows generosity to a saint or god in disguise is rewarded for it.

Q42.4.p: A man frees a slave who turns out to be a disguised prince, and he is rewarded when the slave later becomes king.

Q42.4.1.p: A slave is freed as a reward for killing two of the enemy's slaves, and is also given as much land as he can farm in three days.

Q42.5.p: A ruler rewards a herald who is generous to the ruler's buffoon, or jester.

Q42.6.p: A person who has their eye torn out when asked to is rewarded for complying.

Q42.7.p: A ruler or lord who remits, or forgives, a tribute owed to him is rewarded for doing so.

Q42.8.p: A saint gives a man all of the saint's credit for good deeds so that the man can enter heaven; the saint is then rewarded with even greater credit.

Q42.9.p: A cobbler gives a poor boy a new pair of shoes and says he can pay later, when he becomes archbishop; many years later the cobbler is generously rewarded.

Q43.p: A person who gives good advice is rewarded for it.

Q44.r: Scala Celi 81b, 83a Nos. 465, 472; Alphabet 298, 302; Crane Vitry 175 No. 96; Spanish: Keller, Espinosa II No. 86, Espinosa Jr. No. 200; Jewish: Neuman; India: Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera I 134, 342, II 1091, 1366; Japanese: Ikeda.
Q44.p: A person who gives alms, or money and goods to the poor, is rewarded.

Q44.1.p: A monk who has given alms is rewarded by having his honor and position restored.

Q44.2.p: A man is pardoned for having short accounts, or missing money, when it turns out he gave the money to the poor as alms.

Q44.3.p: A rupee given away as charity unexpectedly brings back ten rupees.

Q45.r: Scala Celi 51b, 81b, 83b, 104b, 152b, 158a, 164b Nos. 290, 466, 477, 569, 839, 884, 926; Alphabet No. 368; Irish myth: *Cross; Swiss: Jegerlehner Oberwallis 323 No. 95; Spanish: Espinosa III No. 152, Espinosa Jr. Nos. 181f.; Italian Novella: *Rotunda; India: Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera II 455, 989; Africa (Loango): Pechuël-Loesche 110, (Kaffir): Kidd 251 No. 13, (Ekoi): Talbot 208.
Q45.p: A person who offers hospitality to guests is rewarded for it.

Q45.1.r: (Cf. Q42.3.) *Dh II 133ff.; *bin Gorion Born Judas@2 I 366; Scala Celi 39b, 81b Nos. 221, 464, 468; Alphabet Nos. 167, 365, 439; Herbert III 392; Literary treatment: Lowell “Vision of Sir Launfal”.—Irish: Cross, O’Suilleabhain 90; Lithuanian: Balys Index No. 752B*; Spanish: Keller, Espinosa Jr. Nos. 181f.; Greek: Pauly-Wissowa s.v. “Baukis”; India: *Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera II 35; Japanese: Anesaki 251f.; N. A. Indian (Maliseet): Mechling JAFL XXVI 219ff.; Africa (Konnoh): Willans 140.
Q45.1.p: A person who entertains strangers without knowing they are angels, saints, or gods is rewarded for the hospitality.

Q45.1.1.r: (Mormon tradition.) **H. Lee, The Three Nephites: the Substance and Significance of the Legend in Folklore (Albuquerque, New Mexico, 1949).
Q45.1.1.p: Three Nephites, holy figures from Mormon belief, give blessings to a household as a reward for hospitality.

Q45.1.2.p: A king refuses to invite the saint Patrick to a feast. The poor man who does invite him, killing his only cow and using his only meal to feed him, is the one rewarded, as Patrick blesses his wife and son.

Q45.1.3.p: Someone is kind to a saint, and in return the saint promises that neither the host nor his descendants will ever be harmed by poisonous or venomous creatures.

Q45.2.p: Someone who shows hospitality to the devil is repaid for it.

Q45.2.1.r: Estonian, Swedish, and Lithuanian: *Balys Tautosakos Darbai VI 27—31; Cheremis: Sebeok-Nyerges.
Q45.2.1.p: A man rescues a devil from thunder without knowing who he is, and the devil generously rewards him.

Q45.3.p: Someone who shows hospitality to an ascetic, a person living a strict religious life, is rewarded.

Q45.3.1.p: Someone who shows hospitality to a monk is rewarded.

Q45.4.p: A person gives up a desire for revenge as a reward for having shown hospitality to someone.

Q45.5.p: A person who has shown hospitality is repaid when the guest attacks and defeats a destructive enemy on the host's behalf.

Q45.6.p: A person who has shown hospitality is repaid when the guest uses magic to bring food and supplies.

Q46.p: Someone who protects a fugitive, a person fleeing from pursuers, is rewarded.

Q46.1.r: Lithuanian: Balys Index No. 3104, Legends Nos. 198—206; Greek: Frazer Apollodorus II 280 n. 1.
Q46.1.p: Someone who protects a holy person on the run is rewarded.

Q47.p: Someone who is kind to orphans is repaid by their dead parents.

Q51.r: Jewish: *Neuman; Chinese: Eberhard FFC CXX 83, Africa (Wakweli): Bender 87f., (Wute): Sieber 197, (Fang): Tessman 196.
Q51.p: Someone who is kind to animals is rewarded.

Q51.1.r: English: Wells 60 (Sire Gawene and the Carle of Carelyle).
Q51.1.p: A knight covers a foal with his own coat to protect it from a storm.

Q51.2.p: Someone who is kind to a tiger is rewarded.

Q53.r: Icelandic: *Boberg; Jewish: Neuman; India: Thompson-Balys; Japanese: Ikeda.
Q53.p: Someone who rescues another person is rewarded.

Q53.1.p: A king in disguise rewards the person who rescued him from robbers.

Q53.2.p: A poor fisherman is rescued, and his rescuer gives him a magic shirt and information about the robbers he is seeking.

Q53.2.1.p: A rescuer is rewarded with a large catch of fish.

Q53.3.p: A maiden queen offers her hand in marriage to whoever rescues her town.

Q53.3.1.p: A maiden queen offers her hand in marriage and great wealth to a man who frees her from a trap, and he receives both as his reward for rescuing her town.

Q54.p: A person is rewarded for being honest, fair, or keeping their word.

Q54.1.p: A ruler tries to frighten or bribe a judge into ruling wrongly, but the judge refuses and is then given a high position as a reward.

Q54.2.p: A captive knight is set free because he kept his word. He is allowed to leave to gather his ransom or to marry his fiancée, and when he returns to his captor, the captor frees him or pays the ransom.

Q55.p: A person is rewarded for sparing the life of an animal, when that animal is actually an enchanted or transformed person.

Q56.p: A person is rewarded for showing love or loyalty.

Q56.1.p: A ruler rewards a man who loves his captive wife by giving him riches and setting them both free.

Q56.2.p: A ruler rewards captives who love each other by setting them free and making them rich.

Q56.3.p: A queen rewards a man of low birth for his love by appointing him an ambassador.

Q57.p: A person is rewarded for caring for the sick.

Q57.1.p: A person is rewarded for shielding Mary from the gaze of onlookers while she gives birth.

Q60.p: A person is rewarded for other good qualities not covered by the categories above.

Q61.r: (Cf. L200.) Irish myth: Cross; Spanish Exempla: Keller; Jewish: Neuman.
Q61.p: A person is rewarded for refusing to seek personal advancement or honor for themselves.

Q61.1.p: A monk who does not ask to become abbot is chosen for the post anyway, and he receives the bribe money that other ambitious monks paid to win it.

Q61.2.p: The devil spares an abbot because of his humility.

Q62.p: A person is rewarded for being able to keep secrets.

Q64.p: A person is rewarded for enduring patiently over a long time.

Q65.p: A child is rewarded for dutifully caring for or obeying their parents.

Q65.1.r: (Cf. Q151.2.) Africa (Gold Coast): Barker and Sinclair 129 No. 23.
Q65.1.p: A person is rewarded for feeding a stepmother who was ungrateful and unkind to them.

Q66.p: A person is rewarded for being humble.

Q66.1.p: A humble person who does not recognize a saint or god in disguise is rewarded for treating them kindly and modestly.

Q67.p: A king is rewarded for carrying out his royal duties faithfully.

Q68.p: A person who acts with honesty and moral uprightness is rewarded.

Q68.1.p: A person who always tells the truth is rewarded for it.

Q68.2.r: Finnish-Swedish: Hackman FFC VI No. 940*; Lithuanian: Balys Index No. 941*; Chinese: Graham.
Q68.2.p: A person who is honest, especially about money or possessions, is rewarded for it.

Q72.p: A person who remains loyal to someone or something is rewarded.

Q72.1.p: A person who stays loyal to a king is rewarded by the king.

Q80.p: A person is rewarded for some good deed or quality not covered by other categories of reward.

Q81.p: A person who keeps trying steadily despite difficulty is rewarded.

Q81.1.p: A nobleman who keeps persisting is finally given a coveted seat on a reserved bench, which becomes free when one of its current occupants dies.

Q82.r: *Type 326; Penzer VII 120 n. 2; Irish myth: *Cross; Icelandic: Boberg; India: Thompson-Balys; Japanese: Ikeda.
Q82.p: A person who shows fearlessness is rewarded, sometimes by a devil or ghost.

Q82.1.r: Africa (Rozwi): Posselt Fables of the Veld (London, 1929) 39ff., (Thonga): Junod 248ff., Berthoud ZsES XXI 154f. No. 10.
Q82.1.p: A girl who lets a snake coil around her body without fear is rewarded for her courage.

Q82.2.p: A wild animal such as a lion or tiger rewards a man who does not show fear of it.

Q83.p: A person who remains faithful in marriage is rewarded.

Q83.1.r: India: Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera I 845.
Q83.1.p: A wife who remains faithful to her husband is rewarded.

Q84.p: A person who bears pain patiently and without complaint is rewarded.

Q85.p: A person who asks the right or sensible questions is rewarded.

Q86.r: Hdwb. d. Märchens II 66a; India: *Thompson-Balys; West Indies: Flowers 567.
Q86.p: A person who works hard and diligently is rewarded.

Q86.1.p: An ant is rewarded for being industrious: she keeps her stored food safe and dry by airing it in the sun, so she has food all winter.

Q87.r: Irish myth: Cross; Jewish: Neuman, Moreno Esdras.
Q87.p: A person who keeps their chastity or sexual purity is rewarded.

Q87.1.p: A ruler who has been turned down by a maiden in his advances ends up marrying her anyway, as a reward for her chastity.

Q87.1.1.p: After being rebuffed, the ruler arranges for the maiden to marry his highest-ranking knight instead.

Q87.1.2.p: A married woman turns down a king's offer of marriage, and the king honors her husband for her faithfulness.

Q87.1.3.p: A rejected suitor is offered a girl by her mother, and he rewards the girl's refusal of him with a gift of money.

Q87.2.p: A courtier is rewarded for resisting a princess's advances; when her father learns of the affair, he honors the courtier and marries him to his daughter.

Q87.3.p: A nun who has suffered patiently for a long time is rewarded by being made abbess of her convent.

Q88.p: A person is rewarded simply for being highly skilled at their craft or art.

Q88.1.p: Fra Lippo Lippi, a painter, is set free by Moors because of his great skill as an artist.

Q88.2.p: A princess kisses an ugly poet while he sleeps, but she kisses his divine mouth rather than his ugly face.

Q91.p: A person is rewarded for being clever or witty.

Q91.1.p: A princess is given in marriage to a thief who proves to be clever.

Q91.2.r: Makes him a valet. Italian Novella: Rotunda.
Q91.2.p: A king gives a reward to a scullion (kitchen servant) for a witty remark.

Q91.3.p: A king gives a reward for a poem.

Q91.4.p: A correct answer is rewarded with a gold ring, and a message is rewarded with a purse of silver.

Q93.p: A person is rewarded for giving help through supernatural powers.

Q93.1.p: A person is rewarded for bringing rain.

Q93.2.p: A person is rewarded for bringing a dead person back to life.

Q94.p: A person is rewarded for curing someone, whether an illness or an injury.

Q95.p: A musician is rewarded for playing music.

Q95.1.p: A person is rewarded for playing the flute.

Q100.p: A general category covering the kinds of rewards given in tales.

Q101.p: A reward that matches the deed: the payment or recompense is fitting to what the person did.

Q101.1.p: A generous, open-handed girl is blessed with great wealth and prosperity as the reward for her liberality.

Q110.p: Rewards given in the form of material goods, such as money, property or valuables, rather than honors or other favors.

Q111.r: *Roberts 190; Irish myth: *Cross; Spanish: Espinosa Jr. Nos. 132, 181; Jewish; Neuman; Chinese: Graham; Africa (Wakweli): Bender 88.
Q111.p: A reward in which the hero or helper receives riches, such as money, treasure or valuables.

Q111.1.p: The hero is rewarded by being made a business partner of a rich man.

Q111.2.p: A host or someone shown hospitality is repaid with riches as a reward.

Q111.3.p: Someone who helps defeat robbers is rewarded with riches.

Q111.4.p: A gold ring is given as the reward.

Q111.5.p: A giant gives gold, silver and a weapon to someone as reward for good advice.

Q111.6.p: The reward is a treasure, such as a hoard of valuables.

Q111.7.p: The reward is jewels or precious gems.

Q111.8.p: The reward is a large amount of land.

Q112.r: *Types 575, 653; *BP II 131ff., III 45ff.; Christiansen FFC XXIV 99; *Fb “prins og prinsesse” II 876; Icelandic: Egils saga einhenda ok Ásmundar Berserkjabana (FAS III) 366 (one-third of kingdom), Boberg; French Canadian: Barbeau JAFL XXIX 19; Spanish: Espinosa III No. 50; Jewish: Neuman; India: *Thompson-Balys; N. A. Indian (Micmac): Rand 427 No. 80; Africa (Yoruba): Ellis 264.
Q112.p: The reward is half of the kingdom, offered to the hero or helper by a king.

Q112.0.1.p: The reward is a whole kingdom given to the one who performs a deed.

Q112.0.1.1.r: (Cf. Q20.) Irish myth: Cross; Jewish: Neuman.
Q112.0.1.1.p: A kingdom is given as the reward for piety or devout religious conduct.

Q112.0.1.2.p: A kingdom is given as the reward for composing a poem.

Q112.0.1.3.p: A kingdom is given as the reward for finding a princess who was kidnapped.

Q112.0.2.p: The reward is half of someone's property or possessions.

Q112.0.3.p: Two thirds of a kingdom is given as the reward for finding kidnapped princesses.

Q112.0.4.p: A third of the kingdom and the king's daughter are given as the reward for getting a victory-stone during the night.

Q112.0.5.p: A virtuous person is rewarded with a princess's hand in marriage and half the kingdom.

Q112.0.6.p: A person is rewarded with power over the whole world.

Q112.0.7.p: A reward is a royal line of descendants, so that the person's family will become a line of kings.

Q112.1.r: Tuamotu: Stimson MS (z-G. 3/1142, 13/174, 420); Africa (Ganda): Baskerville 1ff., (Hausa): Mischlich 164ff. No. 22, (Bondei): Woodward FL XXXVI 367ff. No. 12.
Q112.1.p: A person is rewarded by being made a chief or leader.

Q112.2.p: A reward is sovereignty, meaning kingly power, for a single hour or day.

Q112.3.p: A person is rewarded with a seat beside the king.

Q113.r: English: Wells 94 (The Taill of Rauf Coilyear); and very frequently in medieval romances.
Q113.p: A person is rewarded by being made a knight.

Q113.0.1.p: A person is rewarded with high honors.

Q113.1.p: A person who gives good advice is rewarded by being appointed an earl.

Q113.2.p: A person is rewarded by being appointed a page, a young servant training for knighthood.

Q113.3.p: A person who is pious is rewarded with a high position.

Q113.4.p: A person is rewarded by being appointed to the priesthood.

Q113.4.1.p: As a reward for keeping the Sabbath, God establishes priests and Levites as an institution.

Q114.p: A person is rewarded with gifts or presents.

Q114.0.1.p: Gifts are given to an advisor.

Q114.1.p: A precious knife and belt are left as a gift on the spearshaft outside the tent of an unknown helper.

Q114.2.p: Gifts are returned as rewards for gifts received.

Q114.3.p: A sword is given as a reward.

Q115.r: *Schoepperle II 420ff., 528 —541; Malone PMLA XLIII 413; Irish myth: *Cross; India: *Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera II 946, 1153.
Q115.p: A person is promised any boon or favor they ask for as a reward.

Q115.1.r: *Schoepperle II 420ff., 528ff.; *Krappe Revue Celtique XLVIII (1931) 94; Cross and Nitze Lancelot and Guenevere (Chicago, 1930) 31ff.; Irish myth: *Cross; India: Thompson-Balys.
Q115.1.p: The king's wife demands the reward of any boon she asks for.

Q115.2.p: A king promises his daughter that she may marry whomever she wishes. The promise is a reward for some service.

Q115.3.p: A person is offered any reward they like and asks only for a son. The reward is a boon, and the request is for a child.

Q116.r: Irish myth: Cross; Icelandic: Boberg; Jewish: *Neuman.
Q116.p: A favorable decree or official ruling is given as a reward.

Q116.1.p: A favorable decree is given as the reward for helping a holy person.

Q121.p: Someone is rewarded with freedom, meaning release from slavery or bondage.

Q121.1.p: Slaves are set free as a reward.

Q135.r: (Cf. Q46.1.) Greek: Frazer Apollodorus II 280 n. 1.
Q135.p: Wine is given as a reward for protecting someone. Twelve jars of very sweet wine are the payment.

Q140.p: Rewards that are miraculous or supernatural in nature, rather than ordinary goods.

Q141.r: (Cf. Q1.) Type 750B; Spanish: Espinosa Jr. No. 181; Japanese: Ikeda.
Q141.p: A man is rewarded by having his cows multiply by magic.

Q141.1.p: Monks who always shared with the poor are rewarded with a supply of flour or bread that never runs out.

Q141.2.r: Africa (Wakweli): Bender 37; S. A. Indian (Toba): Métraux MAFLS XL 27f.
Q141.2.p: A reward in which game animals, such as fish, become plentiful.

Q142.p: A magic treasure is given as a reward for humility.

Q143.r: India: *Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera I 155, 167, 427, 1157, II 604, 671, 775, 904.
Q143.p: A person is rewarded by being reborn into a higher or better state.

Q144.p: A person is rewarded by hearing the voice of God.

Q144.1.p: A hermit who has practiced severe self-denial is rewarded by hearing the voice of God.

Q145.r: (Cf. Q151.) Greek: Fox 158 (Sarpedon); Jewish: Gaster Exempla 222 No. 179, *Neuman, Moreno Esdras (Q151.6).
Q145.p: A person is rewarded with a miraculously long life.

Q145.0.1.p: A person is rewarded with happiness during the last year of their life.

Q145.1.p: A person is rewarded with a miraculously long life for offering hospitality.

Q145.1.1.p: A person who gives someone a drink is rewarded with good health.

Q145.2.p: A person is rewarded with a miraculously long life for their honesty and moral integrity.

Q146.p: A plague or epidemic is ended as a reward for good behavior or piety.

Q147.r: Irish: Cross, Beal XXI 317, O’Suilleabhain 46; Finnish-Swedish: Wessman 1 Nos. 1—3; Spanish: Espinosa Jr. No. 186.
Q147.p: Wonders or supernatural signs happen when a pious person dies.

Q147.1.p: The body of a saint miraculously turns over in its grave to make space for a pious man who is buried beside it.

Q147.2.p: A pope who had fought against wicked nobles is at first refused burial inside a church, but a magic wind blows the doors open, showing he has the right to be buried there.

Q147.3.p: A pious person dies from a kiss sent by God.

Q149.p: A miraculous or magical reward that does not fit any of the more specific categories.

Q149.1.p: An animal's color is changed as a reward for a pious deed.

Q150.p: A person is rewarded by being protected from some disaster.

Q150.1.r: Jewish: Moreno Esdras, *Neuman; Chinese: Eberhard FFC CXX 81f.
Q150.1.p: A person is rewarded by being rescued from a great flood.

Q150.1.1.p: Lot and his family are rewarded by being saved when their city is destroyed.

Q150.2.p: A person is rewarded by having all evil and corruption removed from them.

Q151.p: A person's life is spared as a reward.

Q151.1.p: A charitable man's death is postponed as a reward for his generosity.

Q151.2.r: (Cf. Q65.1.) Africa (Gold Coast): Barker and Sinclair 129 No. 23.
Q151.2.p: Death passes by a man because he fed his stepmother.

Q151.3.p: A hospitable person is saved from death.

Q151.4.p: A faithful old dog, threatened with death, proves its worth and is spared.

Q151.5.p: A humble man is saved from drowning by a miracle.

Q151.6.p: A person's life is spared as a reward for offering hospitality.

Q151.7.p: A person's life is spared as a reward for being upright and honest.

Q151.8.p: A person's life is spared as a reward for bravery and steadfastness. In one version a centurion tells his enemies to kill him rather than try to win him over.

Q151.9.r: Jewish: Moreno Esdras (Q151.5); Chinese: Eberhard FFC CXX 188 No. 128.
Q151.9.p: A person is brought back to life as a reward for good conduct.

Q151.10.p: An honest brahman is spared from being killed by a tiger.

Q151.11.p: A man is saved from lions as a reward for his good deed.

Q151.12.p: A woman who showed compassion is doused with boiling oil, but it does not harm her.

Q151.13.p: Women are rewarded by being allowed to keep their lives because they dance excellently.

Q152.r: Jewish: *Neuman; Chinese: Graham; Hawaii: Beckwith Myth 63, 70.
Q152.p: A city is saved from destruction as a reward for some good deed or virtue.

Q152.1.p: A townsperson's hospitality to strangers saves the whole city from being destroyed.

Q153.p: Nature becomes mild and productive under a good king, with abundant crops and harvests.

Q153.1.p: Under a good king, cows have white heads.

Q154.p: A person is rewarded by being protected from dying by violence.

Q154.1.p: The descendants of a man who endured pain silently are promised they will not die violent deaths.

Q156.p: A pious person is granted victory as a reward for their piety.

Q157.p: Hostages are miraculously saved from escape-related harm as a reward for piety.

Q161.p: A person is cured as a reward for some good deed.

Q161.1.p: A person's lost sight is restored as a reward.

Q161.2.p: A person is cured of a disease as a reward.

Q161.3.p: A hunchback is healed as a reward for kindness.

Q162.p: A person is made invulnerable to harm as a reward for a pious act.

Q170.p: Rewards given by a religious power or for religious reasons, as a category of reward.

Q171.p: A sinner is exempted from the punishment that sin would normally bring, as a reward.

Q171.1.r: Alphabet No. 296; Irish: Beal XXI 332, O’Suilleabhain 101.
Q171.1.p: A sinner is forgiven his sins because of an act of charity or kindness he performed.

Q171.1.1.p: A husband who killed his jealous wife is forgiven, and he atones by building a monastery and becoming a monk in it.

Q172.r: Irish myth: *Cross; Spanish Exempla: Keller; Jewish: *Neuman; India: *Thompson-Balys.
Q172.p: A religious reward in which a person is granted entry into heaven.

Q172.0.1.p: A fairy minstrel asks, as his reward for playing music for a saint, to be admitted to heaven.

Q172.0.2.p: General tales describing the rewards awaiting people in heaven.

Q172.1.r: BP III 474ff.; Reinhard PMLA XL 93; Irish: O’Suilleabhain 105, Beal XXI 333; Lithuanian: Balys Index No. 3727; Spanish: Boggs FFC XC 90 No. 767*.
Q172.1.p: A child is taken up to heaven after offering food to a crucifix.

Q172.2.r: Herbert III 328 No. 9; Irish: Beal XXI 330; Spanish: Keller, Espinosa Jr. No. 182; Jewish: Neuman.
Q172.2.p: A man is admitted to heaven because of a single act of charity.

Q172.2.1.r: Lithuanian: Balys Index No. 802A*; Prussian: Plenzat 46.
Q172.2.1.p: A rich man is judged in heaven, and a single piece of bread he gave to a beggar is weighed on the scales to decide his fate.

Q172.3.r: (Cf. Q520.) *Type 756B; *BP III 463; **Andrejev FFC LXIX 154; English: Wells 114 (Sir Isumbras); Spanish Exempla: Keller.
Q172.3.p: A man is admitted to heaven as the reward for doing penance.

Q172.4.p: A palace is being built in heaven for a pious king.

Q172.4.1.p: Rooms in heaven are prepared for a good man, and a dead miser asks the living man to give him at least one of them.

Q172.5.p: Many sinners are allowed into heaven as the reward for a man writing a hymn.

Q172.6.p: A person gets admission to heaven as the reward for giving up a long life.

Q172.7.p: A man is admitted to heaven because he remitted (cancelled) a tribute owed.

Q172.8.p: The mother of a saint is admitted to heaven.

Q172.8.1.p: A saint goes to heaven every Thursday.

Q172.9.p: A person is raised to divine status as a reward.

Q173.p: A saint is made judge of the dead for the men of Ireland as a reward.

Q174.p: A religious reward in which a person is released from hell.

Q174.1.p: A person is released from hell as the reward for repenting.

Q174.1.1.p: A holy man asks God for the release of sinners' souls from hell as a reward.

Q174.1.1.1.p: A saint asks that on Judgment Day he be allowed to lead out seven damned souls for every hair of his vestment.

Q174.1.1.2.p: God grants a saint that no one buried in any of his churches will go to hell.

Q174.1.1.3.p: God grants a saint the privilege of rescuing two people from hell until the end of the world.

Q174.1.1.4.p: A saint asks that anyone who calls on him at death will escape hell.

Q175.p: A holy person is rewarded by being buried and rising from the dead in the same place.

Q176.p: God rewards a community with peace and good weather because it has passed a good law.

Q190.p: A miscellaneous group of rewards given for good conduct that do not fit other categories.

Q191.p: A good man is rewarded by his family line being blessed or continued.

Q192.p: A child is given as a reward for someone's prayer.

Q193.p: Crowns and palms are given as rewards for virtue or faithful service.

Q195.p: Divine or holy blessings are given as a reward for good conduct.

Q200.p: General heading for tales in which wrongdoing is punished.

Q210.r: Irish myth: Cross; Norwegian: Solheim Register 21.
Q210.p: General heading for tales in which crimes are punished.

Q210.1.p: A person is punished for merely intending a crime, even if it is never carried out.

Q211.p: General heading for tales in which murder is punished.

Q211.0.1.p: God takes revenge for a murder only after thirty years have passed.

Q211.0.2.p: The especially grave wickedness of murdering one's own kin is emphasized.

Q211.0.3.p: An emperor is punished for his many murders by being carried off to hell.

Q211.1.r: (Cf. Q552.2.3.3, Q552.3.1.1, Q553.3.3.) *Types 756B, 761*; *Andrejev FFC LXIX 239; Irish myth: *Cross; Finnish-Swedish: Wessman 19 No. 185.
Q211.1.p: A person who kills a parent is punished.

Q211.2.r: Greek: Frazer Apollodorus I 383 n. 3, Aeschylus Eumenides.
Q211.2.p: A person who kills their mother is punished for it.

Q211.3.r: (Cf. Q414.0.1, Q416.0.2.1, Q596.1.) Italian Novella: *Rotunda; Koryak, American Indian: *Jochelson JE VI 378; Africa (Bankon): Ittman 98.
Q211.3.p: A man who kills his wife is punished for it.

Q211.4.r: (Cf. Q418.2, Q455.1, Q553.5.) *Types 781, 832; Irish: O’Suilleabhain 31, Beal XXI 310; Spanish: Espinosa Jr. Nos. 148f.; Greek: Grote I 160; Jewish: *Neuman; Tuamotu: Stimson MS (T-G. 3/15).
Q211.4.p: A person who murders children is punished for it.

Q211.4.1.p: A queen is banished from the kingdom after poisoning her stepson.

Q211.4.2.p: A mother-in-law murders her son's wives.

Q211.5.p: A person who takes their own life is punished for it.

Q211.6.p: Someone who kills an animal is avenged or made to pay for it.

Q211.6.1.p: A person who flays a live calf is punished for it.

Q211.6.2.p: A person who kills a sacred whale is punished for it.

Q211.7.p: A person who splits another's head open and eats the brains is punished for it.

Q211.8.r: (Cf. Q210.1, Q469.4, Q552.19.2.) Irish myth: Cross; Jewish: Neuman; Eskimo (Smith Sound): Kroeber JAFL XII 177, (Greenland): Rink 157, 222, 469, Holm 47, (Cumberland Sound): Boas BAM XV 62.
Q211.8.p: A person who merely wishes to murder someone is punished for it.

Q211.8.1.p: A wounded king makes those who plotted to kill him pay a fine.

Q211.9.r: (Cf. Q411, Q414.0.13.) Irish myth: *Cross; Icelandic: Boberg; Italian Novella: Rotunda.
Q211.9.p: A person who kills a brother or sister is punished for it.

Q211.9.1.p: God punishes a man who murders his brother-in-law by causing the murderer's sons to die.

Q211.9.2.p: A person who kills a foster brother is punished for it.

Q211.10.p: A person who murders a co-wife, the other wife of the same husband, is punished for it.

Q211.11.r: India: Thompson-Balys; Buddhist myth: Malalasekera II 877.
Q211.11.p: A person who massacres an entire tribe or people is punished for it.

Q211.12.r: Tuamotu: Stimson MS (T-G. 3/818); Easter Island: Métraux Ethnology 385; Tonga: Gifford 53; Maori: Beckwith Myth 474.
Q211.12.p: A person who murders their parents is punished by a member of their own family.

Q211.13.p: A slave who kills an enemy on the owner's order is himself killed.

Q212.p: A person who steals is punished for it.

Q212.1.p: A thief who steals from a dwarf or a witch is punished in revenge for the theft.

Q212.2.p: A person who robs graves is punished for the crime.

Q212.3.p: Theft is punished in a way that explains how people came to sweat.

Q212.4.p: The meat of an animal that was stolen cannot be cooked, no matter how long it is boiled or roasted.

Q213.r: (Cf. Q411.8, Q595.2, R10.) Irish myth: Cross; India: Thompson-Balys.
Q213.p: A person who carries off another against their will is punished for the abduction.

Q215.p: A person who eats human flesh is punished for cannibalism.

Q217.p: A person who betrays their ruler or country is punished for treason.

Q220.r: (Cf. Q457.2, Q458.0.5, Q467.2, Q552.2.3.1.2, Q552.2.3.2.2, Q558.11, Q558.12, Q558.17, Q559.4, Q559.5.) Irish: *Cross, Beal XXI 317, 331, 335; Spanish Exempla: Keller; Jewish: *Neuman; India: *Thompson-Balys.
Q220.p: A person who shows contempt for religion or the sacred is punished for impiety.

Q220.1.r: Finnish-Swedish: Wessman 13 No. 113; Lithuanian: Balys Legends Nos. 719—43, 825f.; West Indies: Flowers 567.
Q220.1.p: A devil torments people who are impious, bringing plagues or suffering on them.

Q220.1.1.p: The devil takes the form of an old woman to punish impious nuns. She introduces them to three youths disguised as girls, which leads to the nuns being seduced, and the nuns are stoned to death.

Q221.p: A person who offends a god personally is punished for the offence.

Q221.1.r: (Cf. Q327.) Irish: Beal XXI 336, O’Suilleabhain 125; Spanish Exempla: Keller; Greek: Grote I 32; India: *Thompson-Balys; Hawaii: Beckwith Myth 132, *190, 233; Easter Island: Métraux Ethnology 141; Society Islands: Henry Ancient Tahiti (Honolulu, 1928) 382; West Indies: Flowers 567.
Q221.1.p: A person who behaves rudely toward a god is punished for the discourtesy.

Q221.1.1.p: A person who is rude to messengers of the gods is punished for the discourtesy.

Q221.2.p: A person who opposes Christ at the crucifixion is punished for it.

Q221.3.r: (Cf. Q551.1.8, Q558.4.) *Loomis White Magic 98f.; Spanish: Keller, Espinosa Jr. No. 190; Jewish: *Neuman.
Q221.3.p: A person who speaks disrespectfully about God or sacred things is punished for blasphemy.

Q221.4.p: A sailor who defies God is shipwrecked as punishment.

Q221.4.1.p: A dam builder boasts that God Almighty could not sweep his completed dam away, and the whole structure then gives way and disappears.

Q221.4.2.p: A man vows to recover a loose boat or go to hell trying, and he goes to hell.

Q221.4.3.p: A party of horsemen held up by bad weather vows to reach town whether God wills it or not, and the earth swallows them up.

Q221.5.p: A person who disobeys God is punished for the disobedience.

Q221.6.p: A person who does not trust God is punished for this lack of faith.

Q221.7.p: Someone who doubts that a goddess has told the truth is punished for that doubt.

Q221.8.p: A person who steals from a water deity is punished for the theft.

Q222.r: (Cf. Q411.11, Q415.7, Q431.13, Q491.1.2, Q499.3, Q551.6.5, Q551.8.2, Q552.17, Q556.6, Q557.7, Q558.5, Q558.14, Q558.17, Q558.18, Q559.9.) Irish: *Cross, O’Suilleabhain 114; Spanish: Espinosa Jr. No. 190; Greek (Herodotus): Classical Philology XXXIX (1944) 179f.; Jewish: Neuman.
Q222.p: A person who defiles or disrespects holy places, such as sacred images or buildings, is punished.

Q222.0.1.p: A stone in a church bleeds as a warning that the church will soon be robbed.

Q222.0.2.p: A building or object that has been desecrated miraculously bleeds.

Q222.1.r: Irish: O’Suilleabhain No. 190; England: Baughman; Heptameron No. 33.
Q222.1.p: A person who desecrates the consecrated host (the bread of Communion) is punished.

Q222.1.1.p: A renegade priest who lets a non-Christian defile the host is put to death for it. In the note, a knight kills the priest.

Q222.2.p: A person who mistreats or insults a crucifix is punished.

Q222.3.p: A person who makes an offensive picture of Jesus on the Cross is punished, along with the artist.

Q222.4.p: A magic storm is sent as punishment for someone who profanes a temple.

Q222.5.p: A person who desecrates a church, shrine, or idol is punished.

Q222.5.1.p: Stones fall in the churchyard and punish those who desecrated the church.

Q222.5.2.p: A magic storm is sent as punishment for someone who desecrates a temple.

Q222.5.3.p: A bold woman who dances naked in a church is struck with leprosy as punishment.

Q222.5.4.p: Thieves who try to steal from a church or shrine are magically unable to leave and instead walk in circles.

Q222.5.5.r: (This is done through power of saint.) Irish myth: Cross; England, Wales, Scotland: Baughman.
Q222.5.5.p: A desecrated church is set on fire by burning straw that a sparrow carries to it.

Q222.5.6.p: A person who beats an idol has his hand stuck to it.

Q222.6.p: A person who desecrates sacred temple vessels or utensils is punished.

Q223.r: (Cf. Q523.7, Q554.2, Q557.7, Q559.4.) Spanish Exempla: Keller; India: *Thompson-Balys.
Q223.p: A person who neglects the required services or worship of the gods (or God) is punished.

Q223.1.r: Köhler-Bolte I 148; Lithuanian: Balys Index No. 3361, Legends Nos. 691f.; Swiss: Jegerlehner Oberwallis 280 No. 47.
Q223.1.p: A person is punished for failing to pray to the gods or God.

Q223.2.p: A person is punished for failing to give thanks to the gods or God.

Q223.3.r: Alphabet No. 782; Greek: Frazer Apollodorus I 305 n. 3; Jewish: Neuman; India: Thompson-Balys.
Q223.3.p: A person is punished for failing to make the required sacrifice to the gods.

Q223.4.r: Scala Celi 47a No. 263; Alphabet No. 175; Spanish Exempla: Keller.
Q223.4.p: A priest is punished for failing to hear a person's confession.

Q223.4.1.p: A priest who lets a woman die without hearing her confession is damned and goes to join the devils after his own death.

Q223.5.p: A person is punished for failing to attend church services.

Q223.6.r: (Cf. Q551.2.2, Q552.14.1.) *Loomis White Magic 99f.; Irish myth: *Cross; England, Scotland, U.S.: *Baughman; Lithuanian: Balys Index No. 3375, Legends Nos. 719—45; Jewish: *Neuman; India: Thompson-Balys.
Q223.6.p: A person is punished for failing to keep the Sabbath holy.

Q223.7.p: A person is punished for failing to attend or observe the Mass.

Q223.7.1.p: The Virgin Mary appears to a woman who had neglected to hear mass; when she wakes from her trance, she finds a piece of her candle (taper) that the Virgin took from her.

Q223.8.p: A person who fails to perform a required penance is punished, and in one case a monk falls ill as a result.

Q223.9.p: A person is punished for failing to fast when required.

Q223.9.1.p: A person who neglects to fast is shown a dragon ready to carry him off to hell.

Q223.9.2.p: A musician is flogged for eating a young goat (kid) on Friday, which was a fast day.

Q223.10.p: A person is punished for failing to study the holy scriptures.

Q223.10.1.p: A person is punished for neglecting to study the Torah.

Q223.11.p: A person is punished for failing to circumcise a child.

Q223.12.p: A person is punished for ending a period of mourning too early or failing to complete it.

Q223.13.p: A religious official is punished for neglecting the duties of his office.

Q223.13.1.p: A monk who neglects to bow down at the canonical hours is expelled from the monastery by a saint and dies on the seventh day.

Q223.13.2.p: A clergyman is fined for not giving a blessing over a finished piece of work.

Q223.14.p: A person who fails to make the customary offering or sacrifice to the gods is punished for the neglect.

Q224.r: (Cf. Q414.0.9.) *Dickson 46 n. 55; *Pauli (ed. Bolte) No. 302; *Krappe “La fille de l’homme riche” Byzantion XVII (1944—45) 339—346; Irish: Beal XXI 334.
Q224.p: A person who betrays the secrets of confession, revealing what was confided to a priest, is punished.

Q225.r: (Cf. Q415.8, Q458.0.5, Q551.10.1, Q552.7, Q552.8, Q552.13.1.2, Q553.1, Q554.3, Q554.4, Q555.1, Q558.1.) Finnish-Swedish: Wessman 18 Nos. 171—173; Spanish Exempla: Keller; Jewish: Neuman.
Q225.p: A person who mocks or ridicules religious teachings is punished.

Q225.1.r: (Cf. Q414.0.8, Q469.7, Q559.11.) Spanish Exempla: Keller.
Q225.1.p: A person who holds a heretical belief contrary to accepted religious teaching is punished.

Q225.2.p: A person who rejects the pagan gods is punished.

Q225.3.p: A person who doubts or rejects the religion of Buddha is punished.

Q226.p: A member of a religious order who leaves it is punished.

Q226.1.r: *Crane Vitry 166 No. 72; Kittredge Englische Studien XIX 177; *Herbert III 60. Cf. Type 756B.
Q226.1.p: A hermit leaves his cell to become a robber and falls to his death, breaking his neck.

Q226.2.p: Rebellious clergy are cast out and turned into pigs.

Q227.p: A person who opposes a holy person is punished.

Q227.1.p: A person who kills a king who is under holy protection is punished.

Q227.1.1.p: A person who imprisons someone under holy protection is punished.

Q227.2.p: A person who looks at a saint's corpse is punished.

Q227.3.p: A saint or hero drives a chariot over a person who has displeased him, killing or crushing them.

Q228.r: Anthony. The pig turns upon him and tramples him severely. Italian Novella: Rotunda.
Q228.p: A glutton who tries to kill an animal dedicated to a saint is punished.

Q231.p: A Brahmin is punished for killing an animal.

Q232.p: A person who changes religious faith is punished.

Q232.1.p: A pagan who converts to Christianity is punished by his own people.

Q232.2.p: A Jew who abandons Judaism is punished for apostasy.

Q232.2.1.p: A Jew is punished for leaving Palestine.

Q233.p: A person who gives in to the devil's temptation is punished for it.

Q235.p: A person who curses is punished for the curse.

Q235.1.r: He is now the man in the moon. (Cf. A751, Q221.3.) U.S.: Baughman.
Q235.1.p: A man is punished for cursing God by being placed in the moon.

Q236.p: A person who deceives the divine emperor is punished.

Q237.p: A person who worships idols is punished.
